page: Microsoft Azure E128-32as_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Easv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server is equipped with 1024.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark database operations falling in the average range. Memory performance is strong, as evidenced by a top 25% PassMark memory score, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidth remain average. For machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds for small LLM models, but performance drops to the bottom 10% for large-scale 70B model text generation due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E128-32as_v7 offers high memory density relative to its compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. However, the absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external storage attachments and limiting its utility for heavy parallel processing or large-scale deep learning.

This configuration is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-bound data processing pipelines. It is also appropriate for moderate web serving and lightweight language model inference tasks that fit within system memory.
